question.text: When evaluating two competing term insurance policies for a client, which combination of criteria is MOST comprehensive for an investment adviser to use?

answer.text: Sum assured (risk cover), premium after health and financial underwriting, coverage tenure, available riders, IRDAI claim settlement ratio, and insurer brand/ability to remain around when the claim arises
Only the premium cost and sum assured, as term insurance is a commodity product with no other differentiators
Only the claim settlement ratio and company brand reputation, since all policies are regulated by IRDAI
Only the maturity value and bonus track record, as these determine the long-term wealth creation potential

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook identifies the core term-insurance factors as sum assured, premium and length of coverage, and the broader online/offline term-plan evaluation criteria as: insurer brand continuity, availability of risk cover for the desired tenure, premium after health and financial underwriting, available riders, and IRDAI claim settlement ratio. Using all of these together gives a comprehensive comparison framework for a term plan. The Trap: Term insurance has no maturity value or bonuses — those are endowment features. Premium-and-sum-assured-only ignores tenure, riders, and claim settlement; brand-and-claim-ratio-only ignores price competitiveness. None of these narrow combinations is comprehensive. Note: Match the coverage tenure to the client's earning span and dependents' need horizon, use IRDAI claim settlement ratio as a key reliability signal, and add only those riders the client actually needs so the premium stays optimised after underwriting.
